1.structure_en: Opening oath: "By" (oath particle) + "the racing horses" (plural noun) + "panting" (how they run).

segments.desc_en: Starts a solemn oath to emphasize the message coming in Ayah 6.
Makes the noun specific ("the"). The "l" sound is pronounced clearly.
Feminine plural noun (singular: عَادِيَة — one charging horse).

sarf.root_meaning: to run swiftly, gallop, charge forward
sarf.word_type_en: Plural noun (doer of the action: "ones who run")

transformation.en: Originally ʿādiwāt from root ع-د-و: the "w" turned into "y" because it comes right after an "i" sound, making it smoother to pronounce (ʿādiyāt).

family.en: whoever crosses the limit
let not your eyes pass beyond
an enemy (one who charges against)

irab.en: Starts with وَ ("By…"), an oath particle that makes the noun after it end in an "-i" sound (genitive). The plural noun means "the galloping warhorses."

insight.title_en: An oath by horses loyal to their master
insight.en: The sūrah opens with a vivid oath by warhorses galloping at full speed for the rider who feeds and trains them — setting up a sharp contrast with human beings in Ayah 6, who receive infinitely more from their Lord yet remain ungrateful.

words.root_meaning: to run swiftly, gallop, charge forward

words.role_en: Describes how the horses are running

segments.desc_en: Names the heavy panting sound coming from a horse's chest as it runs.

sarf.root_meaning: to pant heavily from the chest while galloping
sarf.word_type_en: Verbal noun (names an action/sound)

noun.case_en: Ends in -an (describes the manner of running)

irab.en: Ends in "-an" (accusative) because it describes the manner of the horses' running ("running while panting heavily").

insight.title_en: A sound heard only at maximum effort
insight.en: Ḍabḥ is neither neighing nor calm breathing — Arabic uses it specifically for the rhythmic heave of a horse's chest when it gives every ounce of energy in the charge.

words.root_meaning: to pant heavily from the chest while galloping

2.structure_en: Second oath stage: "And then" + "the spark-strikers" (plural noun) + "striking" (the forceful impact).

words.role_en: Second sworn-by plural noun in the oath

segments.desc_en: Means "and then" — shows the next action follows immediately.
Makes the noun specific ("the"). The "l" sound is pronounced clearly.
Feminine plural noun (singular: مُورِيَة — one horse striking sparks).

sarf.root_meaning: to kindle fire, strike sparks from stone
sarf.root_type_en: Two weak letters (1st letter wāw, 3rd letter yāʾ)
sarf.word_type_en: Plural noun (doer of the action: "ones who ignite sparks")

noun.case_en: Ends in -i (connected to the oath in Ayah 1)

transformation.en: The prefix "mū-" makes the 1st root letter (wāw) stretch into a long "ū" sound: mūriyāt.

family.en: the fire which you kindle
to hide the body of his brother

irab.en: Connected by فَ ("and then") to "the racers" in Ayah 1, so it also ends in "-i" (genitive) as the second part of the oath.

insight.title_en: Sparks flying in the pre-dawn dark
insight.en: First you hear their chests panting (Ayah 1); next you see bright sparks flashing under their hooves as they strike rocky ground in the dark before sunrise (Ayah 2).

words.root_meaning: to kindle fire, strike sparks from stone

words.role_en: Describes the forceful striking of sparks

segments.desc_en: Names the forceful strike of hooves hitting rock to spark fire.

sarf.root_meaning: to strike flint or stone to make sparks
sarf.word_type_en: Verbal noun (emphasizes the action)

irab.en: Ends in "-an" (accusative) to emphasize the forceful action of striking sparks off stone.

insight.title_en: Adding physical impact to the flash of fire
insight.en: Pairing "spark-strikers" with qadḥan lets you both see the spark and hear the crack of hoof against stone.

words.root_meaning: to strike flint or stone to make sparks

3.structure_en: Third oath stage: "And then" + "the raiders" (plural noun) + "at dawn" (when the raid happens).

words.role_en: Third sworn-by plural noun in the oath

segments.desc_en: Means "and then" — shows the next action follows immediately.
Makes the noun specific ("the"). The "l" sound is pronounced clearly.
Feminine plural noun (singular: مُغِيرَة — one raiding horse).

sarf.root_meaning: to sweep down in a swift raid; a deep hollow or cave
sarf.word_type_en: Plural noun (doer of the action: "ones who raid")

noun.case_en: Ends in -i (connected to the oath in Ayah 1)

transformation.en: Originally mughwirāt: the "i" vowel moved onto the letter before it and the middle "w" became a long "ī" — making mughīrāt smooth to say.

family.en: when the two of them were in the cave
or caves
your water sunken deep underground

irab.en: Connected by فَ ("and then") to the oath, so it ends in "-i" (genitive) as the third sworn-by plural noun.

insight.title_en: From night ride to dawn arrival
insight.en: Follow the timeline linked by "and then" (fa-): galloping through the night (Ayah 1) → hooves sparking in the dark (Ayah 2) → launching the raid right at dawn (Ayah 3).

words.root_meaning: to sweep down in a swift raid; a deep hollow or cave

segments.desc_en: Tells when the raid happens — at first morning light.

sarf.root_meaning: dawn, morning light
sarf.word_type_en: Time noun (answers "when?")

family.en: and by the dawn when it breathes
Cleaver of daybreak
a lamp

irab.en: Ends in "-an" (accusative) because in Arabic, time words answering "when?" take an "-an" ending ("at dawn").

insight.title_en: Same rhyme, new role
insight.en: Ayahs 1 and 2 used "-an" words to describe how the horses moved; Ayah 3 keeps the exact same rhythm while telling you when the raid strikes — at dawn.

words.root_meaning: dawn, morning light

4.structure_en: Action shifts to a past verb: "Then they stirred up" + "thereby" + "dust" (direct object).

segments.desc_en: Means "and then" — shows the next action follows immediately.
Past tense verb meaning "stirred up / kicked up" (Form IV).
Attached ending meaning "they (feminine)" — referring to the horses.

sarf.root_meaning: to stir up, rise and billow (dust or clouds)
sarf.word_type_en: Past active verb (Form IV — causative)

verb.meaning_of_form_en: Causative — causing dust to rise into the air

transformation.en: The base past verb is athāra ("he stirred up"). When the "-na" ("they f.") ending attaches, the long "ā" shortens and drops so it is easy to pronounce: atharna.

family.en: and they stir up clouds
and they plowed up the earth
plowing the ground

irab.en: Past active verb ("stirred up") with the attached ending نَ ("they [feminine]") as the subject doing the action.

insight.title_en: Why switch from nouns to verbs in Ayah 4?
insight.en: Ayahs 1–3 used descriptive nouns to paint the horses' enduring qualities; Ayahs 4–5 switch to crisp past verbs ("stirred up", "penetrated") to capture the sudden burst of action.

words.root_meaning: to stir up, rise and billow (dust or clouds)

segments.desc_en: Connects the verb to the means or place ("by that gallop / in that place").
Attached pronoun meaning "it" (referring to the gallop or the dawn raid).

words.sarf_note_en: Made of a preposition (bi- "by") and a pronoun (-hi "it"). Neither changes by a 3-letter root pattern.

irab.en: Preposition بِ ("by / in") joined to the pronoun هِۦ ("it"), linking the dust directly to the horses' charge.

insight.title_en: What does "thereby" (bihi) refer to?
insight.en: Commentators note two vivid meanings: "by means of that gallop" or "in that dawn time/place" — both show the dust cloud rising instantly from the charge.

words.role_en: Direct object (what the horses stirred up)

segments.desc_en: Thick battle-dust kicked up into the air by hooves.

sarf.root_meaning: billowing dust raised by hooves
sarf.word_type_en: Noun (direct object)

irab.en: Direct object of "stirred up", so it ends in "-an" (accusative) — answering "what did they stir up? Dust."

insight.title_en: A curtain of dust filling the horizon
insight.en: Here the "-an" word becomes the direct object: the horses' charge physically raises a wall of dust before they plunge into the center of the ranks.

words.root_meaning: billowing dust raised by hooves

5.structure_en: Climax of the oath scene: "Then they plunged into the middle" + "thereby" + "a crowd/host" (direct object).

segments.desc_en: Means "and then" — shows the next action follows immediately.
Past tense verb meaning "cleaved right into the middle of."
Attached ending meaning "they (feminine)" — the horses.

sarf.root_meaning: middle, center, heart of something; balanced
sarf.word_type_en: Past active verb (Form I — base verb)

verb.meaning_of_form_en: To charge straight into the center of a crowd

conjugation_table.verb_lemma_en: to charge into the center of

rows.future_en: you all will cleave the center

family.en: a justly balanced nation
the middle prayer
the most moderate of them

irab.en: Past active verb ("penetrated the center") with the attached pronoun نَ ("they [feminine]") as the subject.

insight.title_en: Fearless loyalty straight into danger
insight.en: Horses naturally shy away from noisy crowds, yet out of loyalty to their rider they plunge straight into the middle of the enemy host — completing the 5-verse oath before the pivot to human ingratitude.

words.root_meaning: middle, center, heart of something; balanced

segments.desc_en: Means "while carrying the riders" or "cloaked in that dust."
Attached pronoun referring back to the dust cloud or the charge.

words.sarf_note_en: Preposition (bi-) + attached pronoun (-hi). Fixed words with no 3-letter root pattern.

irab.en: Preposition بِ ("with / in") joined to the pronoun هِۦ ("it"), attached to the verb "penetrated."

insight.title_en: Still shrouded in dust as they hit the center
insight.en: Repeating bihi links Ayah 5 directly to the dust cloud of Ayah 4: before the dust has even settled, the horses have reached the middle of the host.

segments.desc_en: An assembled gathering or troop of people.

sarf.root_meaning: to gather, assemble into one group
sarf.word_type_en: Collective noun (direct object)

family.en: the Day of Assembly
the multitude will be defeated
who amassed wealth

irab.en: Direct object of "penetrated", ending in "-an" (accusative) — answering "what did they cleave the center of? An assembled host."

insight.title_en: The crescendo before the verdict
insight.en: With jamʿan, the five-verse oath hits its dramatic peak. Now comes the thunderous verdict in Ayah 6.

words.root_meaning: to gather, assemble into one group

6.structure_en: Answer to the oath: "Indeed" (emphasis) + "mankind" + "to his Lord" (possessive Iḍāfa: Lord + his) + "is surely ungrateful" (second emphasis + description).

words.role_en: Strong emphasis particle opening the verdict

segments.desc_en: Strong emphasis particle that makes the next noun ("mankind") end in "-a".

words.sarf_note_en: Particles never change form and do not come from a 3-letter root.

irab.en: Emphasis particle ("Indeed / without doubt") opening the answer to the five-verse oath. It causes its subject ("mankind") to end in "-a".

insight.title_en: Emphasis stacked on a fivefold oath
insight.en: After five verses of oath, the verdict opens with inna ("Indeed") and seals its predicate with la- ("surely") — triple emphasis for a truth human beings rarely want to admit.

words.role_en: Subject of "Indeed" (who the sentence is about)

segments.desc_en: Refers to the human race as a whole.
The human being as a species.

sarf.root_meaning: to be sociable, familiar, at ease; also linked by some scholars to forgetfulness
sarf.word_type_en: Singular noun referring to the human species

family.en: Indeed mankind is in loss
Man was created of haste
he noticed a fire on the Mount

irab.en: The subject of إِنَّ ("Indeed"), so it ends in "-a" (accusative).

insight.title_en: The warhorse vs. the human being
insight.en: A horse risks its life for a handful of grain given by its rider; yet a human being receives life, breath, mind, and provision from his Lord and still forgets his blessings.

words.root_meaning: to be sociable, familiar, at ease; also linked by some scholars to forgetfulness

idafa.explanation_en: The noun رَبِّ ("Lord, Caretaker") connects directly to the possessive pronoun هِۦ ("his"). This highlights the irony: man is ungrateful not to a stranger, but to his own Caretaker.

segments.desc_en: Preposition "to", making the noun "Lord" end in "-i".
The Master and Nurturer, linked directly to "his" in a possessive pair.
Attached possessive pronoun meaning "his."

sarf.root_meaning: to nurture, care for, sustain, and own
sarf.root_type_en: Doubled root (2nd & 3rd letters are both ب)
sarf.word_type_en: Singular noun in a possessive pair (Muḍāf)

transformation.en: The two "b" letters merge under one shadda (ّ), carrying both the 2nd and 3rd root letters in one doubled sound.

family.en: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds
as they raised me when I was small
devoted scholars of the Lord

irab.en: Preposition لِ ("to") + noun رَبِّ ("Lord", ends in -i) + possessive pronoun هِۦ ("his"). Placed before "ungrateful" to highlight who is being wronged.

insight.title_en: Why put "to his Lord" before "ungrateful"?
insight.en: Moving "to his Lord" earlier in the sentence — and using the intimate possessive "his Lord" — puts the Creator's tender care right next to human ingratitude.

words.root_meaning: to nurture, care for, sustain, and own

segments.desc_en: Adds a second layer of emphasis ("surely / truly") to the statement.
A strong descriptive noun meaning chronically ungrateful (like barren soil).

sarf.root_meaning: barren soil that yields nothing; deeply ungrateful
sarf.word_type_en: Intensive descriptive noun (pattern faʿūl = habitual, deep trait)

irab.en: لَ ("surely") adds strong emphasis to كَنُودٌ ("ungrateful"), which ends in "-un" as the main predicate describing mankind.

insight.title_en: Barren earth that drinks rain and gives nothing back
insight.en: In classical Arabic, kanūd described barren soil that drinks the rain yet grows nothing. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī explained: al-kanūd is the one who counts his troubles and forgets his blessings.

words.root_meaning: barren soil that yields nothing; deeply ungrateful

7.structure_en: Second emphasized statement: "And indeed, he" + "to that" + "is surely a witness."

segments.desc_en: Connects this phrase to the previous one ("and").
Strong emphasis particle starting a second verdict.
Attached pronoun meaning "he" (referring back to mankind).

words.sarf_note_en: Three short building blocks joined together: "and" (wa-) + "indeed" (inna) + "he" (-hu). None use a 3-letter root pattern.

irab.en: Connector وَ ("and") + emphasis particle إِنَّ ("indeed") + attached pronoun هُۥ ("he") acting as the subject of the sentence.

insight.title_en: A witness against himself
insight.en: Deep down, man's own conscience, habits, and words testify to his ingratitude even when he tries to make excuses.

segments.desc_en: Links "witness" to what is being witnessed ("witness to that").

words.sarf_note_en: Fixed preposition ("upon / to") — never changes form.

irab.en: Preposition meaning "upon / to", linking the word "witness" to "that."

insight.title_en: Bearing witness "upon" an undeniable fact
insight.en: In Arabic, witnessing ʿalā something means standing over an open, undeniable reality.

segments.desc_en: Points back to man's ingratitude mentioned in Ayah 6.
Adds weight and distance ("that" rather than "this").
Addresses the listener directly.

words.sarf_note_en: Pointer words ("this / that") are fixed words and do not come from a 3-letter root.

irab.en: Pointer pronoun ("that") following the preposition عَلَىٰ ("to"), pointing back to man's ingratitude.

insight.title_en: Highlighting the weight of ingratitude
insight.en: Saying "that" (dhālika) rather than "this" gives gravity to how glaring human ingratitude really is.

segments.desc_en: Adds a second layer of emphasis ("surely / truly") to the statement.
Means an ever-present, undeniable witness.

sarf.root_meaning: to witness firsthand, be present, testify
sarf.word_type_en: Intensive descriptive noun (pattern faʿīl = constant trait)

family.en: and Allah is Witness over all things
Allah witnesses
and the prophets and witnesses will be brought

irab.en: لَ ("surely") emphasizes شَهِيدٌ ("a witness"), which ends in "-un" as the main predicate.

insight.title_en: Why shahīd instead of shāhid?
insight.en: Shāhid is someone who happens to see something once; shahīd (pattern faʿīl) is an ongoing, undeniable witness whose own life is permanent proof.

words.root_meaning: to witness firsthand, be present, testify

8.structure_en: Third emphasized statement with a 2-word possessive link: "And indeed, he" + "in love of wealth" (Iḍāfa pair) + "is surely intense."

segments.desc_en: Connects this phrase to the previous one ("and").
Strong emphasis particle introducing the root cause of ingratitude.
Attached pronoun meaning "he" (mankind).

words.sarf_note_en: Compound of "and" (wa-) + "indeed" (inna) + "he" (-hu). Fixed words with no 3-letter root pattern.

irab.en: Connector وَ ("and") + emphasis particle إِنَّ ("indeed") + pronoun هُۥ ("he") as the subject.

insight.title_en: Exposing the root cause of ingratitude
insight.en: Why is man ungrateful to his Lord (Ayah 6)? Ayah 8 pinpoints the reason: his consuming attachment to wealth.

words.role_en: First word of the "of" pair ("love of wealth")

idafa.mudaf_ilayhi_en: wealth / good (second word — always ends in -i)
idafa.explanation_en: Two words linked in an "of" relationship (Iḍāfa): حُبِّ ("love of") binds directly to the next word ٱلْخَيْرِ ("wealth"). Because it is the first word in the pair, حُبِّ drops "al-" and tanwīn.

segments.desc_en: Means "because of / in his love of…", making "love" end in "-i".
First word in the possessive link ("love of wealth").

sarf.root_meaning: to love deeply; also a seed or core (ḥabba)
sarf.root_type_en: Doubled root (2nd & 3rd letters are both ب)
sarf.word_type_en: Action noun in a possessive pair (Muḍāf)

noun.definiteness_en: Made definite by "wealth" right after it

transformation.en: The two "b" letters merge under one shadda (ّ), carrying both the 2nd and 3rd root letters.

family.en: and you love wealth with immense love
like a grain of seed that sprouts seven ears

irab.en: Preposition لِ ("because of / in") + noun حُبِّ ("love of", ends in -i). It links directly to the next word ٱلْخَيْرِ ("wealth") as a 2-word Iḍāfa pair.

insight.title_en: Ḥubb and ḥabba — the seed planted in the heart
insight.en: Ḥubb (love) shares its root with ḥabba (a seed/core): whatever you love settles into the core of your heart and grows until it steers your whole life.

words.root_meaning: to love deeply; also a seed or core (ḥabba)

words.role_en: Second word of the "of" pair ("love of wealth")

idafa.mudaf_ilayhi_en: wealth / good (completes the "of" phrase, ends in -i)
idafa.explanation_en: Completes the 2-word "of" link with حُبِّ ("love of wealth"). The second word in an Iḍāfa always takes the "-i" (genitive) ending.

segments.desc_en: Makes the noun specific ("the"). The "l" sound is pronounced clearly.
Second word in the "of" pair ("love of wealth"), ending in "-i".

sarf.root_meaning: good, benefit, wealth
sarf.word_type_en: Singular noun completing a possessive pair (Muḍāf Ilayhi)

noun.case_en: Ends in -i (always genitive as 2nd word in Iḍāfa)

family.en: if he leaves behind wealth
Indeed I loved the love of good/horses

irab.en: Second word of the possessive pair ("love of wealth"), so it automatically takes the "-i" ending (genitive).

insight.title_en: Why does the Qur'ān call wealth al-khayr ("good")?
insight.en: Arabic uses al-khayr for wealth both because people view money as the ultimate good, and because wealth itself can be good — until greed makes a person tight-fisted.

words.root_meaning: good, benefit, wealth

segments.desc_en: Adds a second layer of emphasis ("surely / truly") to the statement.
Means fiercely gripped, intense, and tight-fisted.

sarf.root_meaning: to tie tightly, grip hard, be intense or stingy
sarf.root_type_en: Doubled root (2nd & 3rd letters are both د)
sarf.word_type_en: Intensive descriptive noun (pattern faʿīl)

family.en: and We strengthened his kingdom
Indeed the grip of your Lord is severe

irab.en: لَ ("surely") emphasizes شَدِيدٌ ("intense"), which ends in "-un" as the main predicate of the sentence.

insight.title_en: Shadīd — knotted tight with greed
insight.en: Shadda means to pull a knot tight: because of his love of wealth, man becomes tightly knotted, unyielding, and stingy.

words.root_meaning: to tie tightly, grip hard, be intense or stingy

9.structure_en: Wake-up question shifting to present active, then past passive: "Then does he not know" + "when" + "is overturned" (passive verb) + "what is in the graves" (plural noun).

segments.desc_en: Turns the sentence into a pointed wake-up question.
Means "then / so", linking back to man's ingratitude.
Negates the verb right after it ("does he not know?").

words.sarf_note_en: Three short particles joined into one word: question (a-) + "then" (fa-) + "not" (lā). Particles do not have a 3-letter root.

irab.en: Combines a question marker أَ, the connector فَ ("then"), and negation لَا ("not") to ask: "Then does he not know?!"

insight.title_en: Three short particles that jolt the sleeper awake
insight.en: A-fa-lā packs a question, a consequence, and a negation into four letters: "After all this, does he still not realize?!"

segments.desc_en: Present tense verb with an implied subject "he" (mankind).

sarf.root_meaning: to know with certainty
sarf.word_type_en: Present active verb (Form I — base verb)

verb.meaning_of_form_en: To know and realize a truth clearly

family.en: No! Soon you will know
taught man what he did not know
Knower of the unseen and seen

irab.en: Present tense active verb ending in "-u" (normal statement form). The subject "he" (mankind) is understood inside the verb.

insight.title_en: The only present-tense verb in Surah Al-ʿĀdiyāt
insight.en: Yaʿlamu is the sole present-tense verb in the whole sūrah — addressing man in his living present moment right now, while there is still time to wake up.

words.root_meaning: to know with certainty

words.role_en: Time word ("when" — for a certain future event)

segments.desc_en: Used in Arabic for future events that are guaranteed to happen.

words.sarf_note_en: Fixed time word ("when") — does not follow a 3-letter root pattern.

irab.en: Time word ("when") introducing a certain future moment — the Day the graves are overturned.

insight.title_en: Why "when" (idhā) instead of "if" (in)?
insight.en: Arabic uses in ("if") for uncertain possibilities, and idhā ("when") for events guaranteed to arrive.

segments.desc_en: Passive verb with an "u–i" vowel pattern meaning "turned upside down and emptied out."

sarf.root_meaning: to turn upside down and scatter out what was buried
sarf.word_type_en: Past passive verb from a 4-letter root

verb.meaning_of_form_en: Turning a grave upside down so everything buried inside spills out
verb.tense_en: Past form (used in Arabic for future certainty)

passive.label_en: Past Passive (It / He) — In this Ayah

sarf.scholarly_note_en: Classical scholars noted that the 4-letter root b-ʿ-th-r blends baʿatha ("to resurrect") and athāra ("to stir up" — echoing Ayah 4!).

family.en: and when the graves are overturned
then We revived you after your death

irab.en: Past passive verb ("is overturned / scattered out"). The doer is left unnamed for awe; what receives the action is the next word مَا ("what is in the graves").

insight.title_en: The echo between "stirred up" (Ayah 4) and "overturned" (Ayah 9)
insight.en: Just as the horses stirred up the earth's dust in Ayah 4, the earth itself will be overturned in Ayah 9 — and the passive voice conveys sudden, unstoppable command.

words.root_meaning: to turn upside down and scatter out what was buried

segments.desc_en: Stands for everything resting inside the graves.

words.sarf_note_en: Fixed pronoun ("what / that which") — does not follow a 3-letter root pattern.

irab.en: Pronoun meaning "what / that which", acting as the subject receiving the passive verb "is overturned."

insight.title_en: Why "what" (mā) instead of "who" (man)?
insight.en: Inside the grave, bodies have turned into dust and bones ("what is in the graves") before being restored into living people.

segments.desc_en: Means "deep inside", making the next noun ("the graves") end in "-i".

words.sarf_note_en: Fixed preposition ("in") — does not change form.

irab.en: Preposition meaning "in / inside", causing "the graves" after it to end in "-i".

insight.title_en: From deep underground into the open
insight.en: Fī ("deep inside") contrasts sharply with buʿthira ("turned inside out"): nothing buried in the ground stays hidden.

segments.desc_en: Makes the noun specific ("the"). The "l" sound is pronounced clearly.
Broken plural of قَبْر ("grave").

sarf.root_meaning: to bury in the earth; a grave
sarf.word_type_en: Broken plural noun (singular: قَبْر)

family.en: then caused him to die and gave him a grave

family.ar: وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبْعَثُ مَن فِى ٱلْقُبُورِ
family.en: and Allah will resurrect those in the graves

irab.en: Plural of قَبْر ("grave"). Ends in "-i" (genitive) because it comes right after the preposition فِى ("in").

insight.title_en: The twin vaults: graves and chests
insight.en: Both al-qubūr ("the graves", Ayah 9) and al-ṣudūr ("the chests", Ayah 10) share the exact same broken-plural pattern (fuʿūl): one hides the body, the other hides intentions, and both will be opened.

words.root_meaning: to bury in the earth; a grave

10.structure_en: Second passive scene: "And is extracted" (passive verb) + "what" + "is in" + "the breasts/chests" (plural noun).

segments.desc_en: Connects this phrase to the previous one ("and").
Form II passive verb ("u–i" vowels) meaning "extracted, sorted out, and exposed."

sarf.root_meaning: to extract the true kernel, peel away the husk, sum up
sarf.word_type_en: Past passive verb (Form II — doubled middle letter)

verb.meaning_of_form_en: Thoroughly extracting the core truth from every outward excuse
verb.tense_en: Past form (used for guaranteed future certainty)

conjugation_table.verb_lemma_en: to extract, bring out the core

passive.label_en: Past Passive (It / He) — In this Ayah

irab.en: Connector وَ ("and") + past passive verb حُصِّلَ ("is extracted and sorted"). What gets extracted is the next word مَا ("what is in the chests").

insight.title_en: Shelling the nut to expose the kernel
insight.en: In Arabic, taḥṣīl means cracking away a husk to pull out the core inside. On Judgment Day, outward excuses fall away and the true inner motives in the chest are brought out.

words.root_meaning: to extract the true kernel, peel away the husk, sum up

segments.desc_en: Refers to every hidden intention, belief, and secret inside the chest.

words.sarf_note_en: Fixed pronoun ("what / that which") — no 3-letter root pattern.

irab.en: Pronoun ("what / that which") acting as the subject receiving the passive verb "is extracted."

insight.title_en: The unseen contents of the heart
insight.en: In this life people judge by appearances; on that Day, what was hidden inside the chest becomes the decisive record.

segments.desc_en: Means "inside", making the next noun ("the breasts") end in "-i".

words.sarf_note_en: Fixed preposition ("in") — does not change form.

irab.en: Preposition ("in / inside"), causing "the breasts / chests" after it to end in "-i".

insight.title_en: Hidden in clay vs. hidden in the chest
insight.en: Repeating fī ("inside") mirrors Ayah 9 directly: what is inside the graves and what is inside the chests will both come out together.

segments.desc_en: Makes the noun specific ("the"). The "l" blends into the next letter.
Broken plural of صَدْر ("chest / breast").

sarf.root_meaning: chest, breast, forefront
sarf.word_type_en: Broken plural noun (singular: صَدْر)

family.ar: يَعْلَمُ خَآئِنَةَ ٱلْأَعْيُنِ وَمَا تُخْفِى ٱلصُّدُورُ
family.en: He knows the stealthy glance and what the breasts hide
Did We not expand for you your chest?
That Day people will proceed forth in scattered groups

irab.en: Plural of صَدْر ("chest / breast"). Ends in "-i" (genitive) because it follows the preposition فِى ("in").

insight.title_en: Why is there a shadda on ṣād in al-ṣudūr?
insight.en: The doubled "ṣ" comes from "al-" blending into the sun-letter ṣād (aṣ-ṣudūr), while the root is the regular 3-letter root ص-د-ر.

words.root_meaning: chest, breast, forefront

11.structure_en: Grand finale with double emphasis and two possessive links: "Indeed" + "their Lord" (Iḍāfa) + "about them" + "that Day" (Iḍāfa) + "is surely All-Aware."

words.role_en: Strong emphasis particle sealing the sūrah

segments.desc_en: Seals the sūrah with emphatic certainty about God's complete awareness.

words.sarf_note_en: Fixed emphasis particle — does not follow a 3-letter root pattern.

irab.en: Emphasis particle ("Indeed") causing the next noun ("their Lord") to end in "-a".

insight.title_en: Naming the One behind the passive verbs
insight.en: After the unnamed doer of "is overturned" and "is extracted" in Ayahs 9–10, Ayah 11 reveals Who commands that Day: "Indeed, their Lord…"

idafa.explanation_en: Joins رَبَّ ("Lord") directly to هُم ("their") in a possessive pair (Iḍāfa). Notice the shift from singular "his Lord" in Ayah 6 to plural "their Lord" here as all humanity stands resurrected.

segments.desc_en: Subject after "Indeed" (ends in -a), linked directly to "their."
Attached plural possessive pronoun meaning "their."

sarf.root_meaning: to nurture, sustain, own, and hold accountable
sarf.root_type_en: Doubled root (2nd & 3rd letters are both ب)
sarf.word_type_en: Singular noun in a possessive pair (Muḍāf)

transformation.en: The two "b" letters merge under one shadda (ّ), carrying both the 2nd and 3rd root letters.

family.en: Indeed mankind to his Lord is ungrateful
To your Lord, that Day, is the final place

irab.en: رَبَّ ("Lord") ends in "-a" as the subject of إِنَّ ("Indeed"), and joins with the possessive pronoun هُم ("their") in an Iḍāfa pair.

insight.title_en: From "his Lord" (Ayah 6) to "their Lord" (Ayah 11)
insight.en: Ayahs 6–8 spoke of "man" in the singular ("his Lord"); once all graves and chests are opened in Ayahs 9–10, the pronoun expands to the plural ("their Lord") as every generation stands together.

words.root_meaning: to nurture, sustain, own, and hold accountable

segments.desc_en: Connects "All-Aware" to "them" ("All-Aware about them").
Attached plural pronoun meaning "them."

words.sarf_note_en: Preposition (bi-) + plural pronoun (-him). Fixed words with no 3-letter root pattern.

irab.en: Preposition بِ ("about") joined to the pronoun هِمْ ("them"), placed early to emphasize that no one is missed.

insight.title_en: Placed early for focus
insight.en: Putting "about them" right beside "their Lord" reassures us that not a single person or hidden deed goes unnoticed.

words.role_en: Time phrase in an "of" link ("on the Day of that event")

idafa.mudaf_ilayhi_en: that [moment] (the "-in" ending stands in for the entire scene of Ayahs 9–10)
idafa.explanation_en: Combines يَوْمَ ("on the Day of") with إِذٍ ("that moment") in one Iḍāfa word. The "-in" ending acts as shorthand for the omitted clause: "on the Day when the graves are overturned and the chests are exposed."

segments.desc_en: Time word ending in "-a", linked directly to "that moment."
Its "-in" ending stands in for the whole resurrection scene just described.

sarf.root_meaning: a day or momentous time
sarf.word_type_en: Time noun linked in an Iḍāfa compound

family.en: Master of the Day of Judgment
That Day it will report its news

irab.en: Compound time phrase: يَوْمَ ("on the Day of") linked in Iḍāfa to إِذٍ ("that moment"), where the "-in" ending summarizes Ayahs 9–10.

insight.title_en: Two whole verses compressed into two syllables
insight.en: Instead of repeating "on the Day when the graves are overturned and the chests are exposed", Arabic compresses the entire scene into the "-in" ending of yawma-idhin!

words.root_meaning: a day or momentous time

segments.desc_en: Adds a second layer of emphasis ("surely / truly") to the statement.
Means deeply, intimately aware of hidden inner realities.

sarf.root_meaning: to know the hidden inner truth thoroughly; news/report
sarf.word_type_en: Intensive Divine Attribute (pattern faʿīl)

family.en: and Allah is All-Aware of what you do
the Subtle, the All-Aware
That Day it will report its news

irab.en: لَّ ("surely") emphasizes خَبِيرٌۢ ("All-Aware"), which ends in "-un" as the concluding predicate of the sūrah.

insight.title_en: Why end with Khabīr ("All-Aware") rather than ʿAlīm ("All-Knowing")?
insight.en: ʿIlm is broad knowledge, whereas khibra (Khabīr) is intimate knowledge of what lies hidden beneath the surface — answering Ayah 10 ("what is inside the chests is extracted") with precision.

words.root_meaning: to know the hidden inner truth thoroughly; news/report
